artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Phantom Birds is the eighth studio album by English comedian and musician Matt Berry, released in September 2020 on Acid Jazz Records. The album showcases Berry's eclectic approach to songwriting, blending progressive rock sensibilities with elements of jazz, funk, soul, and blues. Across thirteen tracks, the record demonstrates his versatility as both a vocalist and instrumentalist, with compositions ranging from the introspective "Something In My Eye" to the funk-inflected "Man Of Doom" and the bluesy "Hail To The King."

The album's sonic palette reflects Berry's continued exploration of genre-blending arrangements, moving beyond straightforward rock into more sophisticated harmonic territory. The track listing reveals a carefully constructed narrative arc, punctuated by the brief "Intermission," which divides the album's first and second halves. Songs like "Phantom Birds," "You Danced All Night," and "Waving Goodbye" display melodic sensibility alongside the album's more experimental moments, while the closing "Covered In Clowns" provides a characteristically idiosyncratic conclusion.

As Berry's eighth full-length release, Phantom Birds continues his established pattern of artistic independence and genre experimentation. The album represents a mature work from an artist who has consistently resisted commercial categorization, instead pursuing a distinctive vision that draws from multiple musical traditions. Released during a period of relative isolation, the record stands as a testament to Berry's sustained creative output and his commitment to the progressive and eclectic musical direction he has maintained throughout his recording career.
